exercises.heading: 17.2. Exercises
exercises.instruction: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 Solve the differential equation or initial-value problem using the method of undetermined coefficients.
11 and 12 Graph the particular solution and several other solutions. What characteristics do these solutions have in common?

image.alt: Details The image consists of a visual representation of a graph. Six curves are graphed on the horizontal and a vertical coordinate plane. the curve on the first quadrant starts from the top left of the first quadrant, it goes down to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the fourth quadrant, it again goes up to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the first quadrant, it again goes down to the right and ends at the bottom right of the first quadrant. The right curve on the second quadrant starts from the top right of the second quadrant, it goes down to the right and intersects the vertical axis. the curve then enters in the first quadrant, it goes down to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the fourth quadrant, it again goes up to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the first quadrant, it again goes down to the right and ends at the bottom right of the first quadrant. The left curve on the second quadrant starts from the top left of the second quadrant, it goes down to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the third quadrant, it again goes up to the right and intersects the vertical axis. the curve goes up to the right and touches the horizontal axis. The curve again goes down to the right and again goes up to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the first quadrant, it again goes down to the right and ends at the bottom right of the first quadrant. The upper curve on the third quadrant starts from the top left of the third quadrant, it goes down to the right. the curve again goes up to the right and passes through the origin. The curve then goes down to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. It again goes up to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. It again goes down to the right and ends at the bottom right of the first quadrant. The lower curve on the third quadrant starts from the bottom right of the third quadrant. It goes up to the right and passes through the origin. The curve then enters in the first quadrant. It again goes down to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the fourth quadrant, it again goes up to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the first quadrant, it again goes down to the right and ends at the bottom right of the first quadrant. The curve on the fourth quadrant starts from the bottom left of the fourth quadrant, it goes up to the right and touches the horizontal axis. The curve then goes down to the right. It again goes up to the right and intersects the horizontal axis. The curve then enters in the first quadrant, it again goes down to the right and ends at the bottom right of the first quadrant.

solution.paragraph: The solutions are all asymptotic to $$y_{p} = \frac{1}{10}\cos x + \frac{3}{10}\sin x$$ as $$\left. x\rightarrow\infty \right.$$ . Except for $$y_{p}$$ , all solutions approach either $$\infty$$ or $$- \infty$$ as $$\left. x\rightarrow - \infty \right.$$ .

exercises.instruction: 13, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18 Write a trial solution for the method of undetermined coefficients. Do not determine the coefficients.

solution.paragraph: $$y_{p} = \left( {Ax + B} \right)e^{ x}\cos x + \left( {Cx + D} \right)e^{ x}\sin x$$
$$y_{p} = Axe^{ x} + B\cos x + C\sin x$$
$$y_{p} = xe^{- x}{\lbrack{({Ax^{2} + Bx + C})\cos 3x + {({Dx^{2} + Ex + F})}\sin 3x}\rbrack}$$

exercises.instruction: 19, 20, 21 and 22 Solve the differential equation using undetermined coefficients and variation of parameters.
23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 28 Solve the differential equation using the method of variation of parameters.

solution.paragraph: $$y = c_{1}\sin x + c_{2}\cos x + \sin x\ln\left( {\sec x + \tan x} \right) - 1$$
$$y = \left\lbrack {c_{1} + \ln\left( {1 + e^{- x}} \right)} \right\rbrack e^{ x} + \left\lbrack {c_{2} - e^{- x} + \ln\left( {1 + e^{- x}} \right)} \right\rbrack e^{2x}$$
